results.description:
The English firm of William Cooper and Nephews produced this pressed metal sign, in the shape of a legless merino ram, to advertise its product - dipping powder. It is a rare example of nineteenth century point-of-sale advertising. The merino ram was also used on the firm's packaging. 
Dipping powderCooper's Dipping Powder was imported from England and was one of the many brands of dipping preparations available to New Zealand farmers in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The powder was diluted in water, and then animals were dipped into it to control sheep scab, ticks, lice, and other organisms that affected the health of stock and production of wool. Scab was an infectious disease that spread from Australia and was the major animal health problem in New Zealand from the early 1840s to early 1890s.
